facts.text: Chignik, whose Alutiiq name means 'big wind', sits on the Gulf of Alaska and has long been a fishing community.
The Hume Company opened a cannery in 1896, and the Columbia River Packers Association later built Alaska's oldest continuously operating seafood facility in 1910.
The surrounding terrain bears volcanic influences from the Aleutian Range, part of the Aleutian volcanic arc, with Aniakchak Caldera about 43 miles southwest.
Chignik averages 127 inches of rain and 58 inches of snow each year, making it one of Alaska's wettest communities.
On April 17, 1911, a gale blew ashore several ships, including the Benjamin F. Packard, Star of Alaska, and the Jabez Howes.
Chignik's subarctic climate is milder than other Alaskan towns like Fairbanks or Fort Yukon.
